requirement.title: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly
requirement.text:
#### Bug description

Both `MessagePackGenerator` (CS8785) and `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer` (AD0001) throw `IndexOutOfRangeException` when a `[MessagePackObject]` type has a member whose type is a **closed generic value type defined in a referenced assembly**.

Because the generator then "will not contribute to the output", the compiling assembly silently ends up with **no generated resolver at all**. It is only a warning, so a normal build looks fine, but trimmed and NativeAOT apps fail at runtime. In our case three assemblies of a large app had been shipping without a resolver across two releases before we noticed.

#### Repro steps

Two projects. `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack;
namespace Lib;

[MessagePackObject]
public partial record struct Item<T>([property: Key(0)] string Key);
```

`app`, with a `ProjectReference` to `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack; using Lib;
namespace App;

[MessagePackObject]
public sealed partial record Cmd([property: Key(0)] string Scope)
{
    [Key(1)] public Item<int> Member { get; init; }
}
```

Then `dotnet build` on `app`. Both projects are in the attached `mp-repro.zip`.

#### Expected behavior

A clean build, with a generated resolver in `app`.
#### Actual behavior

```
CSC : warning CS8785: Generator 'MessagePackGenerator' failed to generate source. It will not
contribute to the output and compilation errors may occur as a result. Exception was of type
'IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the bounds of the array.'.
CSC : warning AD0001: Analyzer 'MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Analyzers.MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer'
threw an exception of type 'System.IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the
bounds of the array.'.
```

`app.dll` contains no `GeneratedMessagePackResolver`.

- Version used: MessagePack 3.1.8
- Runtime: .NET 10 (SDK 10.0.204), Windows 11

#### Additional context

**What triggers it.** `Item` is declared in `lib`, `Cmd` in `app`:

| `Item` declared as | result |
|---|---|
| `record struct Item<T>` | **crash** |
| `struct Item<T>` | **crash** |
| `struct Item` | ok |
| `record struct Item` | ok |
| `class Item<T>` | ok |
| `record class Item<T>` | ok |

So it needs all three of: **generic**, **value type**, **from a referenced assembly**. Moving the identical `Item<T>` declaration into `app` itself makes the crash disappear, which is what makes this specific to metadata symbols.
**Stack trace.**

```
System.IndexOutOfRangeException: Index was outside the bounds of the array.
   at TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo(INamedTypeSymbol formattedType, ISymbol callerSymbol)
   at TypeCollector.CollectGeneric(INamedTypeSymbol type, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 661
   at TypeCollector.CollectCore(ITypeSymbol typeSymbol, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 371
   at TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo(INamedTypeSymbol formattedType, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 1062
   at TypeCollector.CollectCore(ITypeSymbol typeSymbol, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 386
   at TypeCollector.Collect() in TypeCollector.cs:line 300
   at MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.AnalyzeSymbol(SymbolAnalysisContext, ReferenceSymbols, AnalyzerOptions) in MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.cs:line 431
```

`CollectGeneric` line 661 is the closed-generic branch that calls `GetObjectInfo` directly:

```csharp
else
{
    // NOTE: ... closed generic types such as `Foo<string>` are not registered as a formatter.
    this.GetObjectInfo(type, callerSymbol);
```

so `GetObjectInfo` runs against a type that has no syntax. Several diagnostic paths inside it index `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` directly (lines 735, 1009, 1101) instead of using `FirstOrDefault()` the way the neighbouring `GetIdentifierLocation` / `GetLocation` / `GetParameterListLocation` helpers already do, and that collection is empty for a metadata symbol. I did not narrow down which of the three fires.

**Getting the stack trace.** Console output truncates the exceptio

story: The change stops the crash on member types from referenced assemblies. It removes two direct indexes into DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0], and it now silently drops every analyzer diagnostic whose location is not in a source file of the current compilation. It also adds docs and three tests that compile a library to metadata and reference it.

decisions.title: Dependency change in Directory.Packages.props
decisions.oneliner: Dependency and toolchain versions decide which users can build and run the package.
decisions.question: Accept this dependency or toolchain change?
decisions.routed_by: policy rule 'dependency': the reviewer may not decide this

decisions.title: Filter also drops locationless diagnostics for local types
decisions.oneliner: Every analyzer diagnostic now passes through the filter. Any diagnostic with no location, including ones about local types, is silently dropped.
quote: this.reportDiagnostic = reportAnalyzerDiagnostic is null ? null : diagnostic => ReportIfLocatedInCompilation(reportAnalyzerDiagnostic, diagnostic);
decisions.requirement_part: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException
decisions.would_be_wrong_if: No existing TypeCollector diagnostic is ever created with a null location (Location.None) for a type declared in the current compilation.
decisions.question: Is it acceptable that diagnostics with no location, about types in this project, now disappear without any notice?

decisions.title: Third indexing site (line 735) not visibly fixed
decisions.oneliner: The issue names three [0] index sites. The diff changes two, and the site near line 735 is not in the diff.
decisions.would_be_wrong_if: The line-735 site was already safe in this version, or the line numbers cited in the issue refer to the code changed here.
decisions.question: Has anyone checked that no `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` is left elsewhere in TypeCollector?

handled.title: Generator crash fix not explained by the diff
handled.oneliner: The filter only wraps the analyzer callback, and the generator probably passes null for it. The generator's CS8785 is fixed only if the edited ?.Invoke lines are what it hit.
handled.would_be_wrong_if: The generator also passes a non-null reportAnalyzerDiagnostic. In that case the edited lines would explain the generator crash too.
handled.question: Did the new tests fail on the generator path before this fix?
handled.routed_by: low impact or no decision needed

handled.title: Analyzer coverage depends on what the verifier runs
handled.oneliner: The tests use a source-generator verifier. If it does not run MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer, the AD0001 crash is never exercised.
quote: // Run the analyzers and the generator, failing on any diagnostic (the defect surfaced as AD0001 and CS8785).
handled.would_be_wrong_if: CSharpSourceGeneratorVerifier registers the MessagePack analyzers (this fact is outside the diff).
handled.question: Did these tests fail with AD0001 before the fix?
handled.routed_by: low impact or no decision needed

handled.title: Docs claim the defining assembly reports problems
handled.oneliner: The new docs say the defining project reports these problems. NuGet packages built without the MessagePack analyzer report nothing, and the consumer gets a formatter with no warning.
quote: Diagnostics about the members of such a type are reported by the assembly that defines it rather than by the consuming project, so any problem must be fixed there.
handled.would_be_wrong_if: Every assembly that defines a [MessagePackObject] type is always built with the MessagePack analyzer enabled.
handled.question: Do you want this design note in the README and the MsgPack004 docs, since the bug fix did not ask for it?
handled.routed_by: low impact or no decision needed

handled.title: Unkeyed-member test asserts the silencing
handled.oneliner: The test passes because problems with the referenced type are dropped. It does not check that the formatter generated for an invalid type is correct.
handled.would_be_wrong_if: Silently skipping the unkeyed member is the intended behavior for metadata types.
handled.routed_by: low impact or no decision needed

not_checked: The test suite was not run (no .NET SDK on the review host).
Whether any other `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` or `Locations[0]` index remains elsewhere in TypeCollector or the generator.
Which callers pass a non-null reportAnalyzerDiagnostic (generator or analyzer only).
Whether any existing diagnostic uses Location.None on purpose for in-compilation types.
